page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m4.large is a shared, burstable virtual instance designed for entry-level and intermittent compute requirements. Running on the KVM hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates two virtual CPUs backed by a single physical Intel Xeon 8163 core operating at 2.5 GHz, utilizing two threads per core. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, while offering 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache. It lacks local bundled storage, includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and features a baseline network bandwidth allocation of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations reveal that the burstable CPU model and single physical core impose distinct compute boundaries. In stress-ng testing, the instance achieved a single-core score of 1057.79 (bottom 25%) and a multi-core score of 2090.03 (bottom 10%). Standard system evaluations via Geekbench reflect similar boundaries, scoring 870.0 in single-core and 1493.0 in multi-core routines. Memory throughput measures at 16.3 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 14.44 GB/sec for large-block writes, leading to an overall PassMark memory rating of 959.97. Network and application benchmarks record static web serving throughput at 1.48 GB/sec and Redis SET performance at 2.54 million operations per second.

Cost efficiency for the ecs.t5-c1m4.large is primarily achieved through shared hardware resources and fractional compute capacity. The instance provides a practical memory allocation of 8.0 GB for lower-demand tasks without incurring the expense of dedicated core provisioning. However, sustained compute workloads will quickly encounter performance constraints due to the burstable CPU limits and shared physical infrastructure.

Given its hardware topology and baseline throughput limits, ecs.t5-c1m4.large is primarily fitted for lightweight, non-critical workloads. Practical use cases include small-scale staging environments, low-traffic web serving, basic background workers, lightweight automation tasks, and utility services with sporadic CPU utilization patterns.

There is no bundled local storage, no dedicated GPU accelerator, and baseline network throughput is rated at 0 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations indicate low overall processing throughput, with a Geekbench single-core score of 870.0 and multi-core score of 1493.0, alongside an uncached read memory bandwidth of 16.3 GB/sec. The instance delivers cost-effective resource pooling for bursty operational profiles, making it suitable for low-traffic web servers, development environments, and sporadic utility jobs.
